summary: An afterMerge gate failing over a span the tip already held whole digests the tip's own commit, so the prior-attempt record names another writer's diff as the reverted work

per.section: Prior-outcome feedback to the retrying tick

acceptance: a `gate-revert` record's digest names only what this tick added to the tip it reverts from — over a span the tip already held whole it says nothing was added rather than showing the commit it found standing there — so no retry reads a foreign diff as its own prior attempt; the record's other fields, the revert and its ownership guard are unchanged
tests: the afterMerge gate-revert record over a wholly-absorbed span digests no commit the tick did not make
notes: Off note AN-EMPTY-PICK-IS-ABSORBED-NEVER-READ-AS-A-CONFLICT (3). Verified: both legs run the afterMerge stack whenever no conflict, then hand `mergedSha` to `buildGateRevert` (`src/singletonTick.ts:454`, `src/waveMerge.ts:792`, builder `src/priorAttempts.ts:726`, digest `:712`); over a wholly-absorbed span `mergedSha === preCherry`, the equality both legs already read (`src/singletonTick.ts:517`, `src/waveMerge.ts:882`). The revert itself is safe: `resetKeepTo(preCherry)` is a no-op.
